can_do_en: I can order a bento for here or to go, ask for an extra item, say how the food is, and ask the owner to pack up what I can't finish.

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.zh: 馬克，這家便當店在屏東很有名，又便宜又好吃。
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄇㄚˇ ㄎㄜˋ ㄓㄜˋ ㄐㄧㄚ ㄅㄧㄢˋ ˙ㄉㄤ ㄉㄧㄢˋ ㄗㄞˋ ㄆㄧㄥˊ ㄉㄨㄥ ㄏㄣˇ ㄧㄡˇ ㄇㄧㄥˊ ㄧㄡˋ ㄆㄧㄢˊ ㄧˊ ㄧㄡˋ ㄏㄠˇ ㄔ
dialogue.en: Mark, this bento shop is well known in Pingtung. It's cheap and tasty.

dialogue.speaker: 老闆
dialogue.zh: 歡迎光臨！內用還是外帶？
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄏㄨㄢ ㄧㄥˊ ㄍㄨㄤ ㄌㄧㄣˊ ㄋㄟˋ ㄩㄥˋ ㄏㄞˊ ㄕˋ ㄨㄞˋ ㄉㄞˋ
dialogue.en: Welcome! For here or to go?

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.zh: 內用。馬克，菜單在上面。你要雞腿便當還是排骨便當？
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄋㄟˋ ㄩㄥˋ ㄇㄚˇ ㄎㄜˋ ㄘㄞˋ ㄉㄢ ㄗㄞˋ ㄕㄤˋ ˙ㄇㄧㄢ ㄋㄧˇ ㄧㄠˋ ㄐㄧ ㄊㄨㄟˇ ㄅㄧㄢˋ ˙ㄉㄤ ㄏㄞˊ ㄕˋ ㄆㄞˊ ㄍㄨˇ ㄅㄧㄢˋ ˙ㄉㄤ
dialogue.en: For here. Mark, the menu is up there. Do you want the chicken-leg bento or the pork-chop bento?

dialogue.speaker: 馬克
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄌㄠˇ ㄅㄢˇ ㄐㄧ ㄊㄨㄟˇ ㄕˋ ㄓㄚˊ ˙ㄉㄜ ˙ㄇㄚ
dialogue.en: Excuse me, is the chicken leg fried?

dialogue.speaker: 老闆
dialogue.zh: 對，炸的，很香喔！要不要加滷蛋？一顆十塊。
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄉㄨㄟˋ ㄓㄚˊ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄏㄣˇ ㄒㄧㄤ ㄛ ㄧㄠˋ ㄅㄨˋ ㄧㄠˋ ㄐㄧㄚ ㄌㄨˇ ㄉㄢˋ ㄧ ㄎㄜ ㄕˊ ㄎㄨㄞˋ
dialogue.en: Yes, fried, and it smells great! Do you want to add a braised egg? They're ten dollars each.

dialogue.speaker: 馬克
dialogue.zh: 好，我要雞腿便當。麻煩幫我加一顆滷蛋。
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄏㄠˇ ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄠˋ ㄐㄧ ㄊㄨㄟˇ ㄅㄧㄢˋ ˙ㄉㄤ ㄇㄚˊ ˙ㄈㄢ ㄅㄤ ㄨㄛˇ ㄐㄧㄚ ㄧ ㄎㄜ ㄌㄨˇ ㄉㄢˋ
dialogue.en: OK, I'll have the chicken-leg bento. Please add a braised egg for me.

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.zh: 我要一個排骨便當，飯少一點。今天我請你！
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄠˋ ㄧ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄆㄞˊ ㄍㄨˇ ㄅㄧㄢˋ ˙ㄉㄤ ㄈㄢˋ ㄕㄠˇ ㄧ ㄉㄧㄢˇ ㄐㄧㄣ ㄊㄧㄢ ㄨㄛˇ ㄑㄧㄥˇ ㄋㄧˇ
dialogue.en: I'll have a pork-chop bento with a bit less rice. Today it's my treat!

dialogue.speaker: 老闆
dialogue.zh: 好，一共一百八十塊。湯在那邊，自己拿喔。
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄏㄠˇ ㄧ ㄍㄨㄥˋ ㄧ ㄅㄞˇ ㄅㄚ ㄕˊ ㄎㄨㄞˋ ㄊㄤ ㄗㄞˋ ㄋㄚˋ ㄅㄧㄢ ㄗˋ ㄐㄧˇ ㄋㄚˊ ㄛ
dialogue.en: OK, that's 180 dollars altogether. The soup is over there; help yourselves.

dialogue.speaker: 馬克
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄨㄚ ㄓㄜˋ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄐㄧ ㄊㄨㄟˇ ㄧㄡˋ ㄉㄚˋ ㄧㄡˋ ㄒㄧㄤ
dialogue.en: Wow, this chicken leg is big and smells so good!

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄅㄨˋ ㄘㄨㄛˋ ㄔ ˙ㄅㄚ ㄋㄧˇ ㄧㄡˇ ㄔ ㄅㄠˇ ˙ㄇㄚ
dialogue.en: Pretty tasty, right? Did you get enough to eat?

dialogue.speaker: 馬克
dialogue.zh: 有啦，太飽了，我吃不完。老闆，可以幫我包起來嗎？
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄧㄡˇ ˙ㄌㄚ ㄊㄞˋ ㄅㄠˇ ˙ㄌㄜ ㄨㄛˇ ㄔ ㄅㄨˋ ㄨㄢˊ ㄌㄠˇ ㄅㄢˇ ㄎㄜˇ ㄧˇ ㄅㄤ ㄨㄛˇ ㄅㄠ ㄑㄧˇ ㄌㄞˊ ˙ㄇㄚ
dialogue.en: Yes, I'm stuffed. I can't finish it. Excuse me, could you pack it up for me?

dialogue.speaker: 老闆
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄇㄟˊ ㄨㄣˋ ㄊㄧˊ ㄨㄛˇ ㄅㄤ ㄋㄧˇ ㄅㄠ ㄑㄧˇ ㄌㄞˊ
dialogue.en: No problem, I'll pack it up for you.

dialogue.speaker: 馬克
dialogue.zh: 謝謝小美！下次我請你吃夜市的小吃。
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄒㄧㄝˋ ˙ㄒㄧㄝ ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄇㄟˇ ㄒㄧㄚˋ ㄘˋ ㄨㄛˇ ㄑㄧㄥˇ ㄋㄧˇ ㄔ ㄧㄝˋ ㄕˋ ˙ㄉㄜ ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄔ
dialogue.en: Thanks, Xiaomei! Next time I'll treat you to night-market snacks.

dialogue.speaker: 小美
dialogue.zh: 好啊！那我們星期五晚上去吧。
dialogue.zhuyin: ㄏㄠˇ ˙ㄚ ㄋㄚˋ ㄨㄛˇ ˙ㄇㄣ ㄒㄧㄥ ㄑㄧˊ ㄨˇ ㄨㄢˇ ㄕㄤˋ ㄑㄩˋ ˙ㄅㄚ
dialogue.en: Great! Then let's go on Friday night.

vocab.en: boxed meal, bento (rice with a main dish and sides)
measure word for small round things (eggs, candies)
to trouble (someone); 麻煩 + request = 'could you please...'
to wrap; 包起來 = pack up (leftovers, a gift)
to finish; verb + 完 = finish doing it (吃不完 = can't finish eating)
time, occurrence; 下次 = next time

grammar.note_en: 內用還是外帶？ is the first question at any 便當店: 還是 joins the two choices, so the question needs no 嗎. 小美 uses it again: 雞腿便當還是排骨便當？
又便宜又好吃 and 又大又香 put two good qualities of the food side by side. Each 又 goes right before its adjective, with no 很.
幫 + person + verb asks someone to do something for you: 麻煩幫我加一顆滷蛋, 可以幫我包起來嗎？ The owner answers with the same pattern: 我幫你包起來。

pronunciation.note_en: ㄐ, ㄓ and ㄗ all come up here: 雞 ㄐㄧ, 炸 ㄓㄚˊ, 自己 ㄗˋ ㄐㄧˇ, 在 ㄗㄞˋ. In relaxed Taiwan speech ㄓ often drifts toward ㄗ (炸 can sound like ㄗㄚˊ): understand both, but say ㄓ with the tongue tip curled back. Tone pair 3+3: 老闆 ㄌㄠˇ ㄅㄢˇ and 小美 ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄇㄟˇ are said 2+3, the same shape as 排骨 ㄆㄞˊ ㄍㄨˇ.

comprehension.question_en: Where do Mark and Xiaomei eat their bentos?
What does Mark add to his order?
How much do the two bentos cost altogether?
Why does Mark ask the owner to pack up his food?
options_en: He is too full to finish it
He has to go back to work
They each pay for their own

speaking.prompt_en: You are at a bento shop in Pingtung. Answer 內用還是外帶, order a bento by name, ask the owner to add one thing for you, and say what the food is like.
speaking.prompt_zh: 你在屏東的便當店。老闆問你內用還是外帶。請你點一個便當，請老闆幫你加一樣東西，再說說便當好不好吃。
checklist_en: answered 內用 or 外帶
ordered with 我要 + 一個 + the bento's name
asked for something with 幫我 + verb (幫我加…)
described the food with 又…又…
said 老闆 with 3+3 sandhi (ㄌㄠˇ rises like ㄌㄠˊ)

writing.prompt_en: Write 3 or 4 sentences about a bento shop or snack stall you like: where it is, what you usually order, for here or to go, and what it's like (use 又…又…).
writing.prompt_zh: 寫三、四個句子，介紹一家你喜歡的便當店或小吃：在哪裡？你常吃什麼？內用還是外帶？味道怎麼樣？
writing.model_zh: 我家附近有一家便當店，又便宜又好吃。我常常外帶一個排骨便當，飯少一點。老闆人很好，常常幫我多加一點青菜。
writing.model_zhuyin: ㄨㄛˇ ㄐㄧㄚ ㄈㄨˋ ㄐㄧㄣˋ ㄧㄡˇ ㄧ ㄐㄧㄚ ㄅㄧㄢˋ ˙ㄉㄤ ㄉㄧㄢˋ ㄧㄡˋ ㄆㄧㄢˊ ㄧˊ ㄧㄡˋ ㄏㄠˇ ㄔ ㄨㄛˇ ㄔㄤˊ ㄔㄤˊ ㄨㄞˋ ㄉㄞˋ ㄧ ˙ㄍㄜ ㄆㄞˊ ㄍㄨˇ ㄅㄧㄢˋ ˙ㄉㄤ ㄈㄢˋ ㄕㄠˇ ㄧ ㄉㄧㄢˇ ㄌㄠˇ ㄅㄢˇ ㄖㄣˊ ㄏㄣˇ ㄏㄠˇ ㄔㄤˊ ㄔㄤˊ ㄅㄤ ㄨㄛˇ ㄉㄨㄛ ㄐㄧㄚ ㄧ ㄉㄧㄢˇ ㄑㄧㄥ ㄘㄞˋ

culture_en: 便當 comes from the Japanese word bentō and is Taiwan's everyday boxed meal: rice with one main dish, such as a fried chicken leg (雞腿) or a pork chop (排骨), and a few side dishes. Shops ask 內用還是外帶 ('for here or to go?'), and you call the person running a small shop 老闆 (a woman who runs it is often called 老闆娘). 不錯吃 ('pretty tasty') and 有 + verb (你有吃飽嗎？) are everyday Taiwan Mandarin.
